note: The addresses common/reliability.md used to carry, kept OUT of the rule corpus. A shared rule names no product (common/rule-ownership.md), because a rule that cites a product's file is a rule somebody edits whenever that product is worked on — which is half of why every pull request in this family changed the conventions. But the objection that answer has to face is real: anonymise in place and a year later nobody can check the claim. So the story stays in the rule and the address is kept here, where nothing loads it as policy and nobody edits it when a product moves. It is a record of what was true on the audit date, not a live pointer; do not 'correct' a line number in it.
